classification.difficultyReason: Sum both polygonal-end areas and all rectangular side-face areas, distinguishing perpendicular area heights from sloping perimeter lengths.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of each prism.

spec.description: Triangular prism: triangular side lengths 20, 15 and 25; perpendicular triangular height 12 shown by an external vertical dimension arrow; prism length 10. The 20 label is placed on the corresponding rear triangle edge. Solid blue visible edges and dashed red hidden edges. No measurement units are printed.
spec.mathematics: Physical faces and actualview derive every solid/hiddenedge. Sourcegivens/parallel/equalmarkers/dimensionendpoints retained; ordinaryblack/native10ptlabels. Labels on homologous translated edges denote the same source dimensions; no added right angles or lengths.

sizing.exceptionReason: Supplied source solid starts45mm,50mm where complete diagonal dimensions/labels need space; inspect finalwidthandheight with all native10ptlabels and writing allowances.

answer.worked:
The two triangular ends have total area $2\left(\tfrac12\times25\times12\right)=300$. The rectangular faces have total area $10(20+15+25)=600$.

$S=300+600=900$ square units.

spec.description: Parallelogram prism: cross-section base 3, sloping cross-section side 5, perpendicular height 4, prism length 8. Single and double arrow marks distinguish the two pairs of parallel cross-section edges. Solid blue visible edges and dashed red hidden edges. No measurement units are printed.
spec.mathematics: Physical faces and actualview derive every solid/hiddenedge. Sourcegivens/parallel/equalmarkers/dimensionendpoints retained; ordinaryblack/native10ptlabels. Labels on homologous translated edges denote the same source dimensions; no added right angles or lengths.

answer.worked:
The two parallelogram ends have total area $2(3\times4)=24$. The four rectangular faces have total area $8(3+5+3+5)=128$.

$S=24+128=152$ square units.
